children: Almost 14,000 new units will be delivered in the emirate of Ras Al Khaimah in the UAE over the next two years, property consultancy Cavendish Maxwell said in a report.
This year will see a total of 2,200 handovers, with 600 already delivered in the first half of 2026, followed by 4,700 in 2027 and 7,500 in 2028.

“With 13,800 new homes in the pipeline between now and the end of 2028, upcoming supply is an important factor for the market,” said Yousir Habib, Associate Director at Cavendish Maxwell Ras Al Khaimah,
Increased supply means greater competition between developments, which may lead to more measured price and rental growth, he added.

The opening of Wynn Al Marjan Island – expected in 2027 – will be a key medium-term demand catalyst, potentially supporting tourism inflows, boosting employment and creating additional housing demand, particularly in communities close to Al Marjan Island, the report said.

Rents rose in the first half of 2026, with apartments up 7 percent and villas 8 percent compared to the first half of 2025. Sale prices increased, with apartment and villa prices rising 6.5 percent and 6 percent, respectively.
However, sales prices and rentals have declined slightly over the last three months, indicating early signs of market moderation, the consultancy added.

title: UAE's Ras Al Khaimah emirate to get 14,000 new housing units by 2028
